The CSV export in app/export.py is slow, and exports can reach about 2 million rows, so memory use matters as well as speed. Fix export_orders_csv(db, path) with a minimal change.

Cause: the person who reported this named the per-row customer lookup as the main cause. The function runs `db.query_one("SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = ?", ...)` once per order row, which is an N+1 query pattern. Confirm that in the code before changing it. If you see another large cost, report it and don't fix it unless it is part of the same few lines.

Scope: app/export.py, function export_orders_csv only. Don't restructure the module. Don't touch other files, add dependencies, or create files in the repo. Build only the fix.

Must stay the same:
- The signature export_orders_csv(db, path). Three callers use it.
- The header line and column order: id,customer_name,total,created_at.
- The value formats: total is total_cents/100 with two decimals, created_at is isoformat(), and each row ends with a newline.
- The set of rows written, one per order.
- Customer names can contain commas, so every value must be properly CSV-quoted. Standard-library tools are fine, but check the line endings they produce against the current output.

Required changes:
- Remove the per-row customer lookup. Choose the approach yourself, such as a join or a batched lookup, and say which one you chose and why. It must not load all 2 million rows or build the whole output in memory.
- Write each row to the file as it is produced. Don't build one big string.
- If your approach would change behavior for an edge case, such as an order whose customer is missing, don't decide silently. Report it.

Measure before and after. No timings exist yet, so first write a throwaway benchmark outside the repo, in the scratchpad or a temp directory. It should time export_orders_csv on a synthetic dataset of realistic size and note rough peak memory. Include customer names with commas and quotes. Run it before your change and again after, and report both numbers. If the real db object can't be used, say what you used instead.

Verify:
1. Run the existing tests in tests/test_export.py and show the output.
2. Compare the output file from the old and new code on the same synthetic data. Apart from quoting differences caused by the original's bug with commas, they should be identical. Show the command and its result.
Don't edit the tests to make them pass. If a test fails or looks wrong, report it instead of working around it. Fix the root cause. Don't special-case the test data.

Ask me before: adding any dependency, changing the signature, or touching any file other than app/export.py. Proceed without asking on everything else that is local and reversible.

You're done when the tests in tests/test_export.py pass, the old and new outputs match, the before and after timing and memory numbers are reported, and the diff is confined to export_orders_csv. Finish with a short summary of the change, the numbers, and anything you noticed but left alone.

# app/export.py
def export_orders_csv(db, path):
    rows = db.query("SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents, created_at FROM orders")
    out = "id,customer_name,total,created_at\n"
    for r in rows:
        cust = db.query_one("SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = ?", r.customer_id)
        out += f"{r.id},{cust.name},{r.total_cents/100:.2f},{r.created_at.isoformat()}\n"
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(out)
